current.title: Polarization of a transverse plane wave: linear, circular and elliptical traces, and handedness
current.statement: Let $(E,B)$ be a plane-wave pair of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with wavevector $k\ne0$, angular frequency $\omega>0$ and complex amplitudes $e,b$, and suppose the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] hold, so that $|k|=\omega/c$, $k\cdot e=0$ and $b=k\times e/\omega$. This item is a classification definition for that class of transverse plane waves; it adds no field-theoretic content. Write $e=a+id$ with the real vectors $a=\operatorname{Re}e$, $d=\operatorname{Im}e$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]), so that $k\cdot a=k\cdot d=0$; let $\hat k=k/|k|$, and use $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ and $\times$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. Then: (a) [Trace] At fixed $x$ the electric vector is $E(x,t)=a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$ with $\theta=k\cdot x-\omega t$, and the curve $\gamma(\theta):=a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$ lies in the transverse plane $k^\perp=\{v: k\cdot v=0\}$. It is the image of the unit circle under the linear map $(u_1,u_2)\mapsto u_1a-u_2d$, it is closed with period $T=2\pi/\omega$, and $\gamma(\theta+\pi)=-\gamma(\theta)$. It is called the **polarisation trace** at $x$; the classification below is independent of $x$. (b) [Classification] (i) **Linear polarisation**: $\dim_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{span}\{a,d\}\le1$; the trace is a segment of the line $\mathbb Ra$ traversed twice per period, and $a=d=0$ is the zero wave. (ii) **Circular polarisation**: $|a|=|d|>0$ and $\langle a,d\rangle=0$; the trace is the circle of radius $|a|$ in $k^\perp$, and $|E(x,t)|=|a|$ for all $(x,t)$. (iii) **Elliptical (nondegenerate, noncircular) polarisation**: $\dim\operatorname{span}\{a,d\}=2$ and not (ii); the trace is a nondegenerate ellipse centred at $0$ with the origin in its interior. If $\langle a,d\rangle=0$, the parametrisation is along principal axes and the semiaxes have lengths $|a|$ and $|d|$; the general principal-axis computation is not asserted by this item. (c) [Handedness] For $a,d\in k^\perp$ the cross product $a\times d$ is parallel to $\hat k$, so the **helicity sign** $H:=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle\in\mathbb R$ vanishes exactly in the linear case (i) and is nonzero otherwise ([[def-real-order]] for its sign). This library calls the polarisation **right-handed** when $H<0$ and **left-handed** when $H>0$. Geometrically, $H<0$ means the electric vector at fixed $x$ rotates counterclockwise as seen by an observer facing the incoming wave (looking along $-\hat k$), and $H>0$ means clockwise. This fixes the sign convention of the cited treatment (there: $E_0=\alpha-i\beta$, right-handed iff $\beta=\hat k\times\alpha$, which under $a=\alpha$, $d=-\beta$ is $H=-|a|^2<0$ in the circular case). The names 'right' and 'left' handedness are conventional and both conventions occur in the literature, so later statements in this library use only the sign of $H$. (d) [Status] This is a classification definition: it introduces the trace, the three cases and the sign $H$, and asserts no field equation, no propagation, energy or empirical content. The magnetic amplitude enters only through the transverse relations recalled above.
current.strategy: An explicit classification definition. The transverse conditions $k\cdot a=k\cdot d=0$ are the real and imaginary parts of $k\cdot e=0$ from [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]. The trace formula is the elementary rewriting $\operatorname{Re}\bigl((a+id)e^{i\theta}\bigr)=a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]); closedness and the reflection symmetry are immediate from the circular functions of the encoding definition. In (b)(iii), independence of $a,d$ makes $(u_1,u_2)\mapsto u_1a-u_2d$ injective, so the trace is a linearly embedded circle (an ellipse) around the origin: the origin lies inside because the image of the compact unit circle is a curve encircling $0$ under an injective linear map. In (c), $a\times d$ is orthogonal to $a$ and $d$ and hence parallel to $k$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]), so $H=0$ exactly when $a\times d=0$, i.e. in the linear case; the sign convention is fixed as stated and matches the cited treatment under the dictionary $a=\alpha$, $d=-\beta$. The principal-axis caveat is recorded because the general diagonalisation is not part of this item's strategy. No field equation or physical claim is introduced.
current.physical_scope: Definition-level classification of the polarisation of ideal transverse plane waves satisfying the amplitude conditions of this page, in a named inertial chart with SI units and a fixed wavevector. It fixes the phase convention, the trace, the linear/circular/elliptical cases and the sign of the helicity $H$. Excluded: partially polarised or stochastic light, finite pulses, material media and any empirical claim.

current.title: Polarization, magnetization, bound and free sources, and the fields D and H
current.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its units, its fields $E,B$ and its source densities $\rho,J$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], and let the averaging convention be that of [[post-em-coarse-graining]], in whose sense the objects below are macroscopic.
(a) [Polarization and magnetization] The material model specifies two maps $P,M:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] on the open set $\Omega\times I$: $P$ is the electric dipole moment per unit volume, in $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $M$ the magnetic dipole moment per unit volume, in $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, both read in the frame basis. They are data of the chosen material model: this definition does not compute them from $E$ and $B$, and no relation between $(P,M)$ and the fields is asserted here.
(b) [Bound sources] Write $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ for the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] taken at fixed $t$, and $\partial_t$ for the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] at fixed position, and define the bound charge density and bound current density by $$\rho_b:=-\operatorname{div}P,\qquad J_b:=\partial_tP+\operatorname{curl}M.$$ Since $P,M$ are jointly $C^2$, $\rho_b$ and $J_b$ are continuous (indeed $C^1$); $\rho_b$ carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J_b$ carries $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$.
(c) [Free sources] Define $\rho_f:=\rho-\rho_b$ and $J_f:=J-J_b$, in the same units as $\rho$ and $J$; these are the free charge and free current densities of the model. The decomposition $\rho=\rho_f+\rho_b$, $J=J_f+J_b$ is part of the chosen material model: the same total pair $(\rho,J)$ with a different pair $(P,M)$ is a different model.
(d) [Displacement and magnetic intensity] Define the electric displacement and the magnetic intensity by $$D:=\varepsilon_0E+P,\qquad H:=\mu_0^{-1}B-M,$$ where $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\mu_0,c>0$ are the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; $D$ carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $H$ carries $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-1}$.
(e) [Status] This item fixes objects and the bound/free convention only. No field equation ([[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]]), no constitutive relation ([[post-em-material-closure]]), no conservation of the bound pair ([[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]](a)) and no identification of $P,M$ with microscopic dipole sums is asserted here.
current.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. The regions, fields and sources are those of the named suppliers; the derivatives in (b) are the published divergence, curl and partial derivative; the constants and units are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the $C^2$ class is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the macroscopic reading is the convention of [[post-em-coarse-graining]]. The definition records explicitly that $(P,M)$ are model data read in the laboratory frame basis, that the bound/free split is a modelling choice, and that no constitutive relation between $(P,M)$ and $(E,B)$ is included. Well-definedness of $\rho_b,J_b$ as continuous fields is the componentwise sum/product differentiability calculus of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. No field equation, no derivative of the physical fields and no microscopic interpretation is used.

current.title: Matching units does not determine the permittivity or the response law
current.statement:
(a) [Dimensional exclusion of $E=\varepsilon_0D$] In the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: the electric constant $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ carries $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm C^2\mathrm s^2\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-3}$, the displacement $D$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] carries $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, and the electric field $E$ of [[def-em-fields]] carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$. The product $\varepsilon_0D$ therefore carries $\mathrm F\,\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm C^3\mathrm s^2\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-5}$, which is not the dimension of $E$: the proposed identification $E=\varepsilon_0D$ fails dimensionally in SI and cannot be a field relation of the framework.
(b) [Units do not determine the law] Solving the definition $D=\varepsilon_0E+P$ of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]] gives $E=(D-P)/\varepsilon_0$, which in vacuum ($P=0$) reads $E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}D$. Any proposed law $E=\eta D$ with a constant $\eta>0$ of dimension $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm C^{-1}$ is dimensionally admissible; dimensional consistency therefore does not identify $\eta$, and it does not determine whether the response is local, linear or instantaneous. In the model of [[post-em-material-closure]] the scalar relation is $D=\varepsilon E$, i.e. $\eta=\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ (or $\chi_e=\varepsilon/\varepsilon_0-1$) is fixed by the declared material model, not by units.
(c) [Frequency-domain symbols are not instantaneous coefficients] In the memory branch of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) the response is a causal convolution in time; a scalar $\varepsilon(\omega)$ introduced in the harmonic description acts on the Fourier components of the field history in the material rest frame. The framework therefore does not read $\varepsilon(\omega)$ as an instantaneous multiplicative coefficient in the time domain: doing so silently replaces the convolution by an instantaneous law and is a model-identification error of the same kind as (a).
(d) [Scope] A dimensional and model-identification statement about the framework's own conventions; it asserts no measurement, no material property and no empirical claim.
current.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct dimensional computation and immediate consequences of the definitions. (a): the units of $\varepsilon_0$, $D$ and $E$ are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the derived-unit identities $\mathrm F=\mathrm C\,\mathrm V^{-1}$ and $\mathrm V=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^2\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$ give $\mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm C^2\mathrm s^2\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-2}\mathrm C^{-1}$; multiplying the first by $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ gives $\mathrm F\,\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, a different combination of the base units $\mathrm{kg},\mathrm m,\mathrm s,\mathrm C$. (b): $D=\varepsilon_0E+P$ is a definition of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]], and solving it is elementary algebra; the vacuum constant $\eta=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ has the dimension of $E/D$ while being a model constant. (c): the memory branch is a convolution in time by [[post-em-material-closure]](c); a harmonic symbol acts on Fourier components and does not define an instantaneous coefficient. No physical measurement and no particular material is asserted.

current.title: Planar dielectric interface with prescribed free surface charge
current.statement:
Let the laboratory frame, coordinates $(x,y,z)$ and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $S=\{z=0\}\cap\Omega$ be a stationary planar interface with unit normal $n=e_z$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-=\{z<0\}$ to the side $\Omega_+=\{z>0\}$. Suppose each half-space carries a homogeneous linear dielectric at rest in the laboratory frame in the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]]: constants $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\in(0,\infty)$ with $D=\varepsilon_1E$ on $\Omega_-$ and $D=\varepsilon_2E$ on $\Omega_+$. Let $E,B,D,H$ satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] in a neighbourhood of $S$ with a constant free surface charge density $\sigma_f\in\mathbb R$ and free surface current $K_f=0$. Write $E_{j\,t}$, $E_{j\,n}$ for the tangential and normal parts of the one-sided trace $E_j$ and $D_j$ ($j=1$ on $\Omega_-$, $j=2$ on $\Omega_+$), defined by the Euclidean decomposition against $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:
(a) [Tangential field] $n\times[E]=0$, i.e. $E_{2t}=E_{1t}$: the tangential electric field is continuous across the interface.
(b) [Normal displacement] $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$, i.e. $\varepsilon_2E_{2n}-\varepsilon_1E_{1n}=\sigma_f$, hence $E_{2n}=\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2}E_{1n}+\frac{\sigma_f}{\varepsilon_2}$.
(c) [No free sheet charge] If $\sigma_f=0$, then $\varepsilon_2E_{2n}=\varepsilon_1E_{1n}$ and $E_{2n}=\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\varepsilon_2}E_{1n}$: the normal component is scaled by the positive ratio $\varepsilon_1/\varepsilon_2$, so $E_{2n}$ and $E_{1n}$ have the same sign; $E_{2n}=E_{1n}$ exactly when $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2$. A free surface charge $\sigma_f\ne0$ modifies the normal condition as displayed and is not silently set to zero.
(d) [Magnetic companions] $n\cdot[B]=0$ and, with $K_f=0$, $n\times[H]=0$; for nonmagnetic media with $H=\mu_0^{-1}B$ on both sides this gives $B_{2n}=B_{1n}$ and $B_{2t}=B_{1t}$.
(e) [Scope] A local interface computation under the stated model hypotheses: it solves the electric jump relations against the linear constitutive relations on the two sides and asserts no global field configuration, no existence of the fields, no constitutive law beyond the declared branch and no empirical claim.
current.strategy: **Proof technique:** substitute the constitutive relations into the jump identities of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]. (a)-(b): the theorem gives $n\times[E]=0$ and $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$ pointwise on $S$; decomposing $E_j=E_{j\,t}+E_{j\,n}\,n$ and using $D_j=\varepsilon_jE_j$ from [[post-em-material-closure]] (with the constant scalars $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2>0$) yields the displayed scalar relations, and solving the second for $E_{2n}$ is division by the positive constant $\varepsilon_2$. (c): set $\sigma_f=0$ in (b). (d): the remaining two identities of the theorem; in the nonmagnetic case $H=\mu_0^{-1}B$ on both sides, so $n\times[H]=0$ reads $n\times[B]=0$. The tangential/normal decomposition uses [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) records the scope. Only the jump theorem, the declared constitutive branch and elementary algebra are used.

current.title: Uniform-field dielectric sphere: candidate solution and its class
current.statement:
Let the laboratory frame and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], with spatial coordinates $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, $z=x_3$, $r=|x|$ and the applied field along $e_3$. Fix $a>0$, a field magnitude $E_0>0$ and constants $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\in(0,\infty)$ (the interior and exterior permittivities of the elementary branch of [[post-em-material-closure]], the material being at rest in the laboratory frame), and put $$C:=\frac{3\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}},\qquad d:=\frac{E_0a^3(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}})}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}+2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}}.$$ Consider the time-independent potentials $$\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}(x):=-C\,E_0\,z\quad(r<a),\qquad \varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x):=-E_0\,z+\frac{d\,z}{r^3}\quad(r>a),$$ with fields $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ and $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}E$ inside, $D:=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}E$ outside ($E$ being of the class of [[def-em-fields]] restricted to this time-independent configuration). Write $S=\{r=a\}$ and $n=e_r$ for the outward normal. Then:
(a) [Harmonicity] $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ on $r<a$ and $\Delta\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ on $r>a$ in the classical sense of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and the potentials and their first derivatives extend continuously to the closed sides of $S$.
(b) [Interface conditions] With one-sided traces at $r=a$, $\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,\partial_r\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $S$; equivalently the tangential field is continuous and the normal component of $D$ is continuous, so the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] hold along $S$ in the time-independent reading with $\sigma_f=0$.
(c) [Asymptotics] $\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}(x)+E_0z=dz/r^3$ and $\nabla(\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z)=O(r^{-3})$ as $r\to\infty$: the difference from the applied uniform potential decays like $r^{-2}$ and its gradient like $r^{-3}$.
(d) [Uniqueness in the declared class] Let $(\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}},\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}})$ be $C^2$ on the closed ball $\overline{B_a}$ respectively on every closed exterior region $\{a\le r\le R\}$, harmonic on $r<a$ and $r>a$, satisfying the same interface conditions (b), and satisfying $|\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}+E_0z|\le M/r$ for some $M$ and all sufficiently large $r$. Then $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $\tilde\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}=\varphi_{\mathrm{out}}$. Hence the displayed pair is the unique solution of the dielectric-sphere transmission problem in that class, existence being exhibited explicitly; the uniqueness proof uses only the Green identity, the matching conditions and the decay, with no maximum principle.
(e) [Fields, polarisation and induced dipole] On $r<a$ the field is uniform, $E=C E_0e_3$ with $D=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}CE_0e_3$; outside, the field is that of the applied uniform field plus the field of a point dipole at the origin with moment $p=4\pi\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}\,d\,e_3$; the interior polarisation is $P_{\mathrm{in}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}}-\varepsilon_0)CE_0e_3$ and the bound surface charge density on $S$ is $\sigma_b=n\cdot(P_{\mathrm{in}}-P_{\mathrm{out}})$, the singular coefficient of $\rho_b=-\operatorname{div}P$ at $S$ (with the exterior polarisation $P_{\mathrm{out}}=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{out}}-\varepsilon_0)E_{\mathrm{out}}$).
(f) [Regime and scope] The computation is a quasistatic result of the declared linear branch at $\sigma_f=0$; using $p$ as a dynamic wave polarisability of the sphere requires a separate quasistatic/dipole approximation and is not asserted here. The example asserts no material data and no empirical claim.

current.title: A whole-space plane wave has infinite total energy
current.statement: Fix $K>0$, $\omega:=cK$, $k:=Ke_3$, $E_0>0$ (unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$), the amplitude $e:=E_0e_1$ and $b:=k\times e/\omega=(E_0/c)e_2$, and let $(E,B)$ be the corresponding plane-wave solution of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]) on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with energy density $u$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]; write $\theta(x,t)=Kx_3-\omega t$. Then: (i) [Explicit density] $E=E_0\cos\theta\,e_1$, $B=(E_0/c)\cos\theta\,e_2$ and $u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2\theta(x,t)$, a nonnegative function vanishing exactly on the nodal planes $\cos\theta=0$; the period average at every fixed $x$ is $\langle u\rangle=\varepsilon_0E_0^2/2>0$, uniformly in $x$ and $t$ ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]](a)). (ii) [Unbounded box integrals] Fix $t\in\mathbb R$ and let $R\ge(\omega|t|+\pi/4)/K$. On the sub-box $Q_R:=[-R,R]^2\times[(\omega t-\pi/4)/K,\,(\omega t+\pi/4)/K]$ of the box $[-R,R]^3$ one has $\cos^2\theta\ge1/2$, hence $u\ge\varepsilon_0E_0^2/2$ there; both boxes are product boxes with finite volume ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]]), $u$ is continuous on them and therefore Riemann integrable ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]), and monotonicity of the multidimensional Darboux integral ([[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]) gives $$\int_{[-R,R]^3}u(x,t)\,dx\;\ge\;\int_{Q_R}u(x,t)\,dx\;\ge\;\frac{\varepsilon_0E_0^2}{2}\,\mathrm{vol}(Q_R)\;=\;\frac{\pi\varepsilon_0E_0^2}{K}\,R^2\;\longrightarrow\;+\infty\quad(R\to\infty).$$ Consequently no finite value is attained by the box integrals as $R\to\infty$: the ideal plane wave has infinite total energy in the box-exhaustion sense, in contrast to the total energy of the single-wave 'mode' being finite on any bounded box. (iii) [Contrast with compactly supported data] If instead the constrained data of [[pthm-em-general-wave-ivp]] vanish off a compact set, then by clause (d) of that theorem the fields have compact spatial support at each time, and the instantaneous total energy is the integral of the continuous density $u$ over a compact set, hence finite. So finite total energy is available for decaying data, while the ideal plane wave of (i)-(ii) is not a finite-energy configuration. (iv) [Scope] The example is an exact computation for the ideal plane wave; it reports no measurement, and 'infinite total energy' means the divergence statement (ii), not a claim about any laboratory field or finite beam.
current.strategy: For (i) use $k\times e=(Ke_3)\times(E_0e_1)=KE_0e_2$ and the definitions of $E,B,u$: $u=(\varepsilon_0/2)|E|^2+(1/(2\mu_0))|B|^2=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2\theta$ by $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$, and $\langle\cos^2\rangle=1/2$ is the real-amplitude case of [[lem-em-period-average]] (equivalently (a) of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] with $|e|^2=E_0^2$). For (ii) the range condition on $R$ places $Q_R$ inside $[-R,R]^3$; on $Q_R$, $|Kx_3-\omega t|\le\pi/4$ gives $\cos^2\theta\ge1/2$, and the comparison of integrals is the elementary monotonicity of the multidimensional Darboux integral for continuous integrands over boxes, with $\mathrm{vol}(Q_R)=(2R)^2\cdot\pi/(2K)$ from [[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]]. The bound is $\pi\varepsilon_0E_0^2R^2/K\to\infty$. Part (iii) quotes clause (d) of [[pthm-em-general-wave-ivp]] and the finiteness of the integral of a continuous function over a compact set. No empirical input is used.

current.title: Linear, circular and elliptical amplitude choices
current.statement: Use the frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and SI conventions of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], fix $K>0$, $\omega:=cK$, $k:=Ke_3$ (so $|k|=\omega/c$), and let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$. For each amplitude choice below put $b:=k\times e/\omega$, so that the amplitude equations of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] hold and the corresponding fields are smooth source-free vacuum Maxwell solutions on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. (i) [Linear] $e:=E_0e_1$, $b=(E_0/c)e_2$: here $a=E_0e_1$, $d=0$, the trace is the segment $\{\pm E_0e_1\}$ traversed twice per period, the polarisation is linear and $H=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle=0$; $E=E_0\cos\theta\,e_1$, $B=(E_0/c)\cos\theta\,e_2$, and $|B|=|E|/c$. (ii) [Circular] $e:=E_0(e_1+ie_2)$, $b=(E_0/c)(e_2-ie_1)$: $a=E_0e_1$, $d=E_0e_2$, so $|a|=|d|=E_0$ and $\langle a,d\rangle=0$ (circular polarisation of radius $E_0$); $E=E_0(\cos\theta\,e_1-\sin\theta\,e_2)$, $B=(E_0/c)(\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2)$, $|E|=E_0$ and $|B|=E_0/c$ everywhere, and $H=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle=E_0^2>0$, so this polarisation is left-handed in the convention of [[def-em-polarization-definition]]; the reversed choice $e=E_0(e_1-ie_2)$ gives $H=-E_0^2<0$ and is right-handed. (iii) [Elliptical] $e:=E_0(e_1+2ie_2)$: $a=E_0e_1$, $d=2E_0e_2$ are orthogonal with unequal lengths, so by [[def-em-polarization-definition]](b)(iii) the trace is the axis-aligned ellipse $E_0\cos\theta\,e_1-2E_0\sin\theta\,e_2$ with semiaxes $E_0$ and $2E_0$ along $e_1,e_2$; $|E|^2=E_0^2(\cos^2\theta+4\sin^2\theta)$ varies between $E_0^2$ and $4E_0^2$; $b=(E_0/c)(e_2-2ie_1)$ and $H=2E_0^2>0$. (iv) [Degenerate and edge cases] $e=0$ gives the zero wave. For $e:=E_0(1+i)e_1$ one has $a=d=E_0e_1$, so the polarisation is linear with trace the segment $[-\sqrt2E_0,\sqrt2E_0]e_1$ and $H=0$; the classification (b) of [[def-em-polarization-definition]] covers this case without requiring $a$ and $d$ to be orthogonal. (v) [Verification and scope] In every case $b=k\times e/\omega$ and $|k|=\omega/c$, so the amplitude equations hold and the fields are smooth source-free solutions ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]); the amplitudes and the semi-axis lengths carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $|B|=|E|/c$ pointwise. The examples assert no empirical realisation and no measured polarisation.
current.strategy: Direct substitution: for each choice compute $a=\operatorname{Re}e$, $d=\operatorname{Im}e$, the trace $a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta$, the helicity sign $H=\langle a\times d,\hat k\rangle$ with $\hat k=e_3$, and $b=k\times e/\omega$; then apply the classification clauses (b),(c) of [[def-em-polarization-definition]] and the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]](b). For (ii) the identity $|E|=E_0$ follows from $|a\cos\theta-d\sin\theta|^2=|a|^2\cos^2\theta+|d|^2\sin^2\theta$ when $\langle a,d\rangle=0$ and $|a|=|d|$. For (iv) the trace values are $E_0(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)$, whose range is $[-\sqrt2E_0,\sqrt2E_0]$. Nothing beyond the listed suppliers is used, and no physical interpretation is added.

current.title: Ideal deterministic two-wave interference and its fringe geometry
current.statement: Let $K>0$, $\omega:=cK$, let $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$ (half the angle between the beams) and $\varphi\in\mathbb R$, and take the two plane waves of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with $$k_1=K(\sin\alpha\,e_1+\cos\alpha\,e_3),\qquad k_2=K(-\sin\alpha\,e_1+\cos\alpha\,e_3),$$ $$e_1^{\mathrm{amp}}=E_0e_2,\qquad e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}=E_0e^{i\varphi}e_2,$$ where $E_0>0$ carries $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and both amplitudes are polarised along $e_2$, perpendicular to both wavevectors; with $b_j=k_j\times e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}/\omega$ and $|k_j|=\omega/c$ both pairs satisfy the amplitude equations of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so the superposition is a source-free smooth Maxwell solution ([[pthm-em-classical-interference]]). Write $\delta(x):=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x=-2K\sin\alpha\,x_1$. Then: (i) [Averaged energy density] $\langle u\rangle(x)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\bigl[1+\cos^2\alpha\,\cos(2K\sin\alpha\,x_1+\varphi)\bigr]$ for every $x$, by clause (b) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] with $e_1\cdot\overline e_2=E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}$ and $(\hat k_1\times e_1^{\mathrm{amp}})\cdot(\hat k_2\times\overline{e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}})=E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}\cos2\alpha$. (ii) [Fringes and visibility] At fixed $x_2,x_3$ the averaged energy density is periodic in $x_1$ with period $\pi/(K\sin\alpha)=\lambda/(2\sin\alpha)$, where $\lambda=2\pi/K$; its maximum and minimum are $\varepsilon_0E_0^2(1\pm\cos^2\alpha)$, so the visibility $V:=\frac{\langle u\rangle_{\max}-\langle u\rangle_{\min}}{\langle u\rangle_{\max}+\langle u\rangle_{\min}}$ equals $\cos^2\alpha=\frac12(1+\hat k_1\cdot\hat k_2)$. In particular $V=1$ for copropagating beams ($\alpha=0$, no spatial fringe variation) and $V\to0$ as $\alpha\to\pi/2$ (counterpropagating beams). (iii) [The promised copropagating amplitude law] For $k_1=k_2=k$, equal amplitudes $E_0$ and relative phase $\Delta$ (so that the sum is the single plane wave with amplitude $E_0(1+e^{i\Delta})$), $\langle u\rangle=\varepsilon_0E_0^2(1+\cos\Delta)=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(\Delta/2)\propto|1+e^{i\Delta}|^2$, the form used in the double-slit discussion of the content model. (iv) [Statistical qualifications] This is a deterministic prediction of the classical wave model for the specified coherent two-wave preparation, at every point of the ideal plane-wave field; a *measured* fringe pattern or detector histogram would additionally require a declared measurement model (detector response, finite bin width, background, integration time, sampling) and a statistical analysis. The example reports no observation, no finite-sample claim and no visibility estimate from data; in particular classical electromagnetic waves interfere, so the prediction alone does not discriminate between classical and quantum descriptions of light. All quantities are idealised field quantities of the framework.
current.strategy: Specialise clause (b) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] to the stated amplitudes: $|e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}|^2=E_0^2$, $e_1^{\mathrm{amp}}\cdot\overline{e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}}=E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}$, and and $\hat k_1\times e_2=\sin\alpha\,e_3-\cos\alpha\,e_1$, $\hat k_2\times e_2=-\sin\alpha\,e_3-\cos\alpha\,e_1$ give $(\hat k_1\times e_2)\cdot(\hat k_2\times e_2)=\cos2\alpha$ by the coordinate cross product [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; the formula (i) follows with $W=2E_0^2\cos^2\alpha\,e^{i(\delta-\varphi)}$. Part (ii) reads off the period, maxima, minima and visibility from (i). Part (iii) is clause (c) of [[pthm-em-classical-interference]] with $|a_1e_1+a_2e_2|^2=2E_0^2(1+\cos\Delta)$. Part (iv) is a scope statement: the field-theoretic identities are exact for the specified preparation, and no statistical model or dataset is introduced. No additional supplier is used.

Excluded: real sources and detectors, finite coherence and bandwidth, sampling and noise models, finite-sample statistics, and any empirical claim; no discrimination between classical and quantum descriptions is asserted.

current.title: Declared averaging kernel, macroscopic scale assumptions and averaged fields
current.statement:
Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following coarse-graining convention for matter. Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its units, its fields and its sources be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the smoothing theorem cited in clause (b).
(a) [Averaging length and kernel] Fix an averaging length $\ell>0$ and a nonnegative function $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ in the Euclidean test-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], with $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\eta(x)\,dx=1$; for $\ell>0$ put $\eta_\ell(x):=\ell^{-3}\eta(x/\ell)$ (the scaled family of [[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]] with $n=3$, $\varepsilon=\ell$). The pair $(\ell,\eta)$ is declared data of the model and is held fixed in every statement that uses it.
(b) [Averaged fields] Let $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$ ($m=1$ or $3$) be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]], read at fixed $t$). Extend $F(\cdot,t)$ by zero outside $\Omega$ and define the averaged field by the convolution integral $$F_\ell(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\eta_\ell(x-y)\,F(y,t)\,dy$$ of [[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]] with kernel $\eta_\ell$ (the real case, read componentwise, of its statement for complex $f$). Then $F_\ell$ is defined on $\mathbb R^3\times I$, and by that lemma, for each fixed $t$, the map $x\mapsto F_\ell(x,t)$ is smooth with $\partial_x^\alpha F_\ell=(\partial^\alpha\eta_\ell)*F$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, derivatives being taken under the integral sign; the lemma also gives the absolute existence and measurability of the convolution and its independence of representatives. On the interior region $\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega)>\ell\}$, the value $F_\ell(x,t)$ is the average of $F(\cdot,t)$ over the ball $B_\ell(x)$ against the weight $\eta_\ell(x-\cdot)$.
(c) [Macroscopic reading and scale separation] The framework reads its macroscopic fields and source densities as such averages only in situations where a separation of microscopic and observation scales is stated for the problem at hand; the averaging length is part of that statement, and no canonical value of $\ell$ is asserted. This is a formulation choice for the macroscopic description, not a consequence of the vacuum equations.
(d) [Boundary handling] On the boundary layer $\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\le\ell\}$ the average of (b) also averages the zero extension outside $\Omega$. Any other boundary convention (a declared extension of the microscopic field, an imposed boundary-layer model, or restriction of the macroscopic region to the interior of the layer) is an additional model assumption and must be declared where it is used.
(e) [No constitutive content] Coarse graining reorganises the description; it does not by itself produce a constitutive relation between averaged fields and averaged sources, and no linear, local or instantaneous response is asserted by this postulate. Such a response is the separate assumption [[post-em-material-closure]], and the derivation of macroscopic field equations from the vacuum equations is the separate result [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]].
current.strategy: An adopted nonproof formulation. The test-function convention and the local-integrability notion are those of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]; the convolution integral, its scaled family and its smoothness with differentiation under the integral sign are those of [[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]] (kernel $\eta_\ell$, mass one, input $F(\cdot,t)$), a lemma stated under countable choice, which this postulate declares and uses only in the regularity clause (b). The locally integrable class is that of [[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]]. Clause (d) records the boundary extension explicitly rather than silently; clause (e) records that averaging supplies no constitutive law and no field equation. No proof is supplied and none is claimed, in accordance with the nonproof status of a postulate; the source and scope review covers the formulation, its boundary and scale-separation conventions, and its non-derivation.

current.title: Declared material-closure branches: linear nondispersive Ohmic response and the causal memory branch
current.statement:
Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following constitutive branches for the material described by the macroscopic fields of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]].
(a) [Material rest frame] The relations below are stated in a material rest frame: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the Minkowski model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which the material element under consideration is at rest, with spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; when the material is at rest in the laboratory frame of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the components below are the laboratory components. Boosting the material changes both the fields and the rest observer; this postulate does not assert that the relations below hold with the same constants in every frame.
(b) [Elementary inertial-rest branch] In the rest frame, with constant symmetric positive-definite matrices $\varepsilon,\mu\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ (the isotropic scalar cases $\varepsilon=\varepsilon\mathbf 1$, $\mu=\mu\mathbf 1$ with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ included), the model takes $$D=\varepsilon E,\qquad B=\mu H,\qquad J_c=\sigma E,$$ where $\sigma\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ is symmetric positive semidefinite and $J_c$ is the conduction part of the free current, $J_f=J_c+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ for a declared external free current $J_{\mathrm{ext}}$; local, linear and nondispersive (instantaneous) response is part of this restricted assumption. In the isotropic case an exact broadband interpretation of the constant-coefficient law additionally requires $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$, so that the characteristic speed $1/\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu}$ does not exceed the vacuum speed $c$; without that condition, and in the anisotropic branch, the constant-coefficient law is a declared finite-band effective phase-response model and carries no universal front-speed claim.
(c) [Causal memory branch] Alternatively, and again in the rest frame, the polarisation response to the electric history is the causal convolution $$P(t)=\varepsilon_0\int_0^\infty K(s)\,E(t-s)\,ds$$ for a declared real matrix kernel $K:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ in $L^1(0,\infty)$ ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]); the integral then converges absolutely for bounded continuous histories $E$ because $|K_{jk}(s)E_k(t-s)|\le(\sup|E_k|)|K_{jk}(s)|$. The kernel class actually used, together with causality and passivity, is part of the model and is analysed in [[pthm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]; neither causality nor passivity is automatic. A finitely-subtracted analytic response may instead be declared by a scalar transfer function $\chi$ that is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, of class $C^1$ on the real boundary away from a real subtraction point $\omega_0$, holomorphic on a neighbourhood of $\omega_0$, and satisfies $|\chi(z)|\le C(1+|z|^{n-1})$ on $\{\operatorname{Im}z\ge0\}$ outside a compact set for some integer $n\ge1$ and constant $C>0$ ([[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]).
(d) [Status] These are adopted model assumptions, one branch at a time; the framework does not derive them from the vacuum equations or from coarse graining, and no microscopic mechanism, material data or empirical validity is claimed. Ferroelectric and ferromagnetic response, hysteresis, nonlinear response and general nonlocal response lie outside the branches declared here.

current.title: Specified causal material response: transfer function, dispersion relations and the passivity condition
current.statement:
Assume the memory branch of the material-closure postulate [[post-em-material-closure]] in a material rest frame, and assume the hypotheses of the mathematical suppliers [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]] and [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]]: Countable Choice for the smooth comparison route and, in the integrable branches, Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $E:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be the electric-field history in the material rest frame, read componentwise in its spatial basis ([[def-em-fields]]), and let $P$ be the polarisation response declared by the model.
(a) [Causal response] If the kernel of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) satisfies $K\in L^1(0,\infty;\mathbb R^{3\times3})$, then for every bounded continuous history $E$ the response $P(t)=\varepsilon_0\int_0^\infty K(s)E(t-s)\,ds$ is well defined for every $t$, bounded and continuous, linear in $E$, and causal: histories equal on $(-\infty,t_0]$ produce responses equal on $(-\infty,t_0]$.
(b) [Transfer function and dispersion relations] If $K$ is smooth with compact support in $(0,\infty)$, the transfer function $\chi(z)=\int_0^\infty K(s)e^{izs}\,ds$ is entire, satisfies $\chi(-\omega)=\overline{\chi(\omega)}$ for real $\omega$, obeys $|\chi_{jk}(z)|\le\|K_{jk}''\|_{L^1}|z|^{-2}$ for $z\ne0$ with $\operatorname{Im}z\ge0$ (with the whole-plane bound carrying the exponential factor $e^{b\max(0,-\operatorname{Im}z)}$ when $\operatorname{supp}K\subseteq(0,b)$), and its entries satisfy the principal-value dispersion relations of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]](b). If $K$ is locally absolutely continuous on $[0,\infty)$ with $K,K'\in L^1$ and $sK\in L^1$, then $\chi$ is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, continuous with continuous first derivative on the real boundary, obeys the stated growth bound, and satisfies the same pair of relations; an instantaneous real part $\chi_\infty$ may be added to the model, and the relations apply to $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}-\chi_\infty$ for $\chi_{\mathrm{total}}=\chi_\infty+\chi$.
(c) [Finitely-subtracted and polynomial branches] If the declared response transfer function satisfies the hypotheses of [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]], then the subtracted relations with the explicit Taylor polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\chi^{(j)}(\omega_0)(z-\omega_0)^j/j!$ hold for every integer $n\ge1$; the unsubtracted $n=0$ case ($P=0$, $f=\chi$, growth $O(1/|z|)$, factor $(\omega-\omega_0)^0=1$) is included. The separate constitutive-polynomial branch $\sum_{j=0}^mA_jE^{(j)}+K*E$ with real coefficients or matrices $A_j$ and $K$ as in the supplier is causal on histories with bounded continuous derivatives through order $m$, with transfer function $Q(z)+\chi_K(z)$, $Q(z)=\sum_{j=0}^mA_j(-iz)^j$; subtracting $Q$ leaves the proved relations for $\chi_K$, and $Q$ need not equal the Taylor polynomial $P$.
(d) [Monochromatic work and passivity] For $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^3$, $E(t)=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{-i\omega t})$ and the monochromatic response with transfer matrix $\chi(\omega)$, the period-averaged work per unit volume is $\frac{\varepsilon_0\omega}{2}\operatorname{Im}(e^*\chi(\omega)e)$; it is nonnegative for every $e$ if and only if the Hermitian dissipative part $M(\omega)=(\chi(\omega)-\chi(\omega)^*)/(2i)$ is positive semidefinite. Passivity is therefore an additional model condition, not a consequence of the causality and dispersion clauses; an instantaneous part $\chi_\infty$ contributes the storage term $\tfrac{\varepsilon_0}{2}E\cdot\chi_\infty E$ instead of irreversible averaged work.
(e) [Scope] The response is declared in the material rest frame of [[post-em-material-closure]](a); boosting the material changes the fields and the rest observer, and no frame-independent instantaneous response law is asserted. The framework does not claim that any particular material realises these branches, no microscopic mechanism is derived, and no empirical statement is made.
current.strategy: **Proof technique:** identification of the declared material response with the hypotheses of the two mathematical suppliers, clause by clause, with no independent analytic re-derivation. (a)-(b): the memory-branch kernel classes of [[post-em-material-closure]](c) are literally the hypotheses of clauses (a)-(c) of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]; the identification is $P$ = macroscopic polarisation, $E$ = electric-field history in the rest frame, $\varepsilon_0$ = the framework constant of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and the transfer function is the model's polarisability matrix. Existence, boundedness, continuity, linearity, causality, the entire/holomorphic transfer function, the reality identity, the decay bounds and the principal-value relations are then those of the supplier applied entrywise; no derivative of the physical fields is taken and no additional modelling assumption is used. (c) is exactly the statement of [[lem-em-finitely-subtracted-analytic-dispersion]], including its $n=0$ case and its constitutive-polynomial branch; the coefficients $A_j$ are declared model data, not determined by the framework. (d) is clause (d) of [[thm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]: the period-averaged work formula and the iff-condition on $M(\omega)$. The Choice hypotheses of the suppliers are stated and carried; no stronger choice principle is used. (e) records the frame dependence and the absence of microscopic, material and empirical claims.

current.title: Superposition intensity and the coherent interference cross term
current.statement: Let $\omega>0$ and let $k_1,k_2\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ satisfy $|k_1|=|k_2|=\omega/c$. For $j=1,2$ let $e_j\in\mathbb C^3$ with $k_j\cdot e_j=0$, put $b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$ and let $(E_j,B_j)$ be the plane-wave solutions of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] given by [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]. Let $a_1,a_2\in\mathbb R$ and put $(E,B):=a_1(E_1,B_1)+a_2(E_2,B_2)$. Then: (a) [Superposition] $(E,B)$ is a smooth source-free solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations ([[pthm-em-linear-superposition]]), and at each fixed $x$ it can be written with a single phase, $$E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\alpha(x)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x-\omega t)}),\qquad B(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\beta(x)\,e^{i(k_1\cdot x-\omega t)}),$$ where $\alpha(x):=a_1e_1+a_2e_2e^{i\delta(x)}$, $\beta(x):=a_1b_1+a_2b_2e^{i\delta(x)}$ and $\delta(x):=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$; constant relative phases are absorbed in $e_2$. (b) [Averaged energy density with the coherent cross term] For every $x$, $$\langle u\rangle(x)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{4}|\alpha(x)|^2+\frac{1}{4\mu_0}|\beta(x)|^2=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\bigl(a_1^2|e_1|^2+a_2^2|e_2|^2\bigr)+\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}a_1a_2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(W(x)\bigr),$$ where $W(x):=\bigl(e_1\cdot\overline e_2+(\hat k_1\times e_1)\cdot(\hat k_2\times\overline e_2)\bigr)e^{i\delta(x)}$. The first two terms are the sum of the averaged energy densities of the two waves ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]]); the third is the interference cross term, which for a fixed relative phase does not average away. (c) [Averaged flux and momentum; equal wavevectors] (with $u$ the energy density and $S$ the Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]) $\langle S\rangle(x)=\frac{1}{2\mu_0}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha(x)\times\overline{\beta(x)}\bigr)$. In particular, if $k_1=k_2=:k$ then the superposition is the single plane wave with amplitude $a_1e_1+a_2e_2$, and $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|a_1e_1+a_2e_2|^2$, $\langle S\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|a_1e_1+a_2e_2|^2\hat k$ ([[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]]). (d) [No incoherent or statistical claim] The formulas are deterministic identities for the specified coherent superposition; they are not an ensemble average over phases, and no detection statistics, finite-sample visibility estimate or empirical conclusion is drawn. The computation is a conditional consequence of the adopted Maxwell postulate and does not by itself distinguish classical from quantum descriptions of light.
current.strategy: Clause (a): $E_j,B_j$ are source-free smooth solutions of the vacuum Maxwell postulate by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]](a); the superposition is again such a solution by [[pthm-em-linear-superposition]] (real coefficients). The single-phase rewriting uses $e^{i\theta_2}=e^{i\delta(x)}e^{i\theta_1}$ with $\theta_j=k_j\cdot x-\omega t$ and $\delta=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x$. Clauses (b),(c): at each fixed $x$ write $E=\operatorname{Re}(\alpha(x)e^{-i\omega t})$-form and apply the componentwise averages of [[lem-em-period-average]], $\langle\operatorname{Re}(\alpha e^{-i\omega t})\operatorname{Re}(\beta e^{-i\omega t})\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$ and the cross-product version; substituting into $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] and using $|k_j|=\omega/c$, $b_j=k_j\times e_j/\omega$ together with the identity $(k\times u)\cdot(k\times v)=|k|^2u\cdot v$ for $u,v\perp k$ (from [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) gives the displayed cross term with $W$. For $k_1=k_2$ the bracket reduces to $2e_1\cdot\overline e_2$ and the formulas reduce to the single-wave averages of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] for the amplitude $a_1e_1+a_2e_2$. No ensemble or statistical averaging is performed, which is exactly the content of the scope clause (d).

Excluded: ensembles or random phases, partially coherent and finite sources, detection or sampling statistics, any empirical conclusion, and any claim discriminating classical from quantum descriptions.

current.title: Constrained smooth vacuum Maxwell initial-value theory with finite propagation
current.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]. Let $t_0<T$ be real, let $E_0,B_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^\infty$ fields ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on the whole-space laboratory region $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume the constraints $$\operatorname{div}E_0=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B_0=0$$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Put $\dot E_0:=c^2\operatorname{curl}B_0$ and $\dot B_0:=-\operatorname{curl}E_0$. No decay, boundedness, compactness or finite-energy hypothesis is imposed on the data. Then: (a) [Existence and explicit representation] There are jointly $C^\infty$ fields $E,B:\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R^3$ (in the extension sense of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]) satisfying the four smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$, $J\equiv0$ and the initial conditions $E(\cdot,t_0)=E_0$, $B(\cdot,t_0)=B_0$, $\partial_tE(\cdot,t_0)=\dot E_0$, $\partial_tB(\cdot,t_0)=\dot B_0$. Explicitly, each component $E_i$ is the scalar solution $u$ of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](a) with data $(a,b)=(E_{0,i},\dot E_{0,i})$ and $h=0$, each $B_i$ that with $(a,b)=(B_{0,i},\dot B_{0,i})$, in the spherical-mean representation $u=\partial_sH_a+H_b$ of that theorem (the mean being that of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]). (b) [Uniqueness] Every pair of jointly $C^2$ fields on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (in the extension sense) satisfying the same four equations with $\rho\equiv0$, $J\equiv0$ and $E'(\cdot,t_0)=E_0$, $B'(\cdot,t_0)=B_0$ equals $(E,B)$; the time derivatives at $t_0$ are then automatically $\dot E_0,\dot B_0$ by the Ampere and Faraday equations. (c) [Finite propagation and domain of dependence] If a second pair of constrained data $(E_0',B_0')$ agrees with $(E_0,B_0)$ together with all curls on the closed ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ — that is, $E_0=E_0'$, $B_0=B_0'$, $\operatorname{curl}E_0=\operatorname{curl}E_0'$ and $\operatorname{curl}B_0=\operatorname{curl}B_0'$ there — then the corresponding solutions agree at $(x_*,t_*)$, for all $x_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and $t_*\in[t_0,T]$. Consequently the value at $(x_*,t_*)$ is determined by the Cauchy data on the closed backward cone $K(x_*,t_*)=\{(y,v):|y-x_*|\le c(t_*-v)\}$ of [[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]]. In the causal geometry of the adopted affine Minkowski model this cone is the model's causal past cone of the event $(x_*,t_*)$ in the chart $x^0=ct$; by the reachability objects of [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]] and the straight-segment criterion and time monotonicity of [[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]], events outside it cannot be joined to $(x_*,t_*)$ by a future causal path, so the constructed field supplies no vacuum influence outside the model's causal cones; this identification of the PDE cone with the model's causal cone is the modelling statement of the item, not an additional empirical claim. (d) [Compact support] If in addition $E_0$ and $B_0$ vanish off a compact set $K\subset\mathbb R^3$, choose $\rho>0$ with $K\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]); then for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ one has $E(x,t)=B(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$. (e) [Scope] This is the smooth whole-space vacuum branch with initially constraint-satisfying data; no finite-total-energy conclusion is drawn (a general smooth but non-decaying solution may have infinite total energy), and no boundary condition, inhomogeneous source, weak-branch content or empirical claim is asserted. The result is conditional on the adopted postulates and on $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the latter used only through the cited scalar theorem.
current.strategy: Set $\dot E_0=c^2\operatorname{curl}B_0$, $\dot B_0=-\operatorname{curl}E_0$, and solve the six scalar Cauchy problems by [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](a) with data $(E_{0,i},\dot E_{0,i})$ and $(B_{0,i},\dot B_{0,i})$; the $C^\infty$ claim and the explicit representation through the spherical-mean family $H_\varphi=sM_{cs}\varphi$ are clause (a) of that theorem, whose mean is that of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]. Put $R_i:=\partial_tE_i-c^2(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$ and $Q_i:=\partial_tB_i+(\operatorname{curl}E)_i$. Each is $C^\infty$ and solves the homogeneous scalar wave equation: differentiating the component wave equations and commuting derivatives ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) gives $\partial_t^2R_i=c^2\Delta R_i$, $\partial_t^2Q_i=c^2\Delta Q_i$. Initially $R=Q=0$, and $\partial_tR_i(t_0)=c^2\Delta E_{0,i}+c^2(\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}E_0)_i=c^2\nabla_i\operatorname{div}E_0=0$, $\partial_tQ_i(t_0)=c^2\nabla_i\operatorname{div}B_0=0$ by the curl-curl identity [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]] and the constraints. The uniqueness clause [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](b) applied to the zero wave problem gives $R=Q=0$, i.e. the two evolution equations. The constructed fields are smooth and satisfy the evolution equations with $\operatorname{div}E(\cdot,t_0)=\operatorname{div}E_0=0$ and $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t_0)=0$, so the constraint propagation of [[pthm-em-gauss-constraint-propagation]](a) with $\rho=J=0$ gives $\operatorname{div}E\equiv\operatorname{div}B\equiv0$; all four Maxwell equations therefore hold. Uniqueness (b): any other $C^2$ solution has componentwise the same Cauchy data and, by [[pthm-em-vacuum-wave-equation]], satisfies the homogeneous scalar wave equation, so [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](b) identifies it with the constructed field. Clause (c) applies [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](c) componentwise, whose hypothesis is agreement of both scalar data functions on the ball: $E_0$ and $c^2\operatorname{curl}B_0$ for the $E$ components, $B_0$ and $-\operatorname{curl}E_0$ for the $B$ components, exactly the stated hypothesis; the cone reformulation uses the backward-cone object and the causal reachability and future-causal-path conclusions of the two cited SR items as the model's geometric language. Clause (d) applies [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](d) to each component, whose data vanish off $K$ because $E_0,B_0$ and their curls do. No decay or extra regularity is assumed, and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is consumed only inside the cited scalar theorem.

current.title: The macroscopic Maxwell equations in terms of D, H and the free sources
current.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ jointly of class $C^1$ with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and continuous source densities $\rho,J$ of [[def-em-sources]]. Let $P,M$ and the derived objects $\rho_b,J_b,\rho_f,J_f,D,H$ be those of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]], with $P,M$ of class $C^2$, and use the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then:
(a) [Bound-source conservation] $\partial_t\rho_b+\operatorname{div}J_b=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. Consequently $\partial_t\rho_f+\operatorname{div}J_f=\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J$: the free pair is conserved exactly when the total pair $(\rho,J)$ is.
(b) [Macroscopic equations] On $\Omega\times I$, $$\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD.$$
(c) [Interpretation and scope] Equations (b) are an exact rewriting of the adopted vacuum equations under the decomposition of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]]: the two equations written in $E$ and $B$ are unchanged, and the $D$ and $H$ equations hold for every $C^2$ pair $(P,M)$, independently of any constitutive law. The identity of (a) is exactly the statement that the bound source pair constructed from $(P,M)$ is conserved and uses the exchange of $\partial_t$ with $\operatorname{div}$ for $C^2$ data. No claim is made for the weak branch of the Maxwell postulate, for singular or sheet sources or for discontinuous $(P,M)$; no constitutive relation and no empirical statement is made.
current.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, componentwise. (a): from [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]](b), $\operatorname{div}J_b=\operatorname{div}\partial_tP+\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}M$. The second term vanishes: in components $\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}M=\sum_i\partial_i(\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_jM_k)$, and pairwise cancellation of the mixed partials $\partial_i\partial_jM_k=\partial_j\partial_iM_k$ is [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] applied to the $C^2$ components of $M$; the first term equals $\partial_t\operatorname{div}P$ by the same theorem applied to the $C^2$ components of $P$; adding $-\partial_t\operatorname{div}P$ gives zero. Linearity of $\partial_t$, $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ is [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] read componentwise. (b): Gauss's law $\operatorname{div}E=(\rho_f+\rho_b)/\varepsilon_0$ together with $\rho_b=-\operatorname{div}P$ gives $\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon_0E+P)=\rho_f$, i.e. $\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f$. The equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ are unchanged. Ampere's law $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ with $J=J_f+\partial_tP+\operatorname{curl}M$ gives, after dividing by $\mu_0$ and moving $\operatorname{curl}M$ to the left, $\operatorname{curl}(\mu_0^{-1}B-M)=J_f+\partial_tP+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$, where $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}=\varepsilon_0$; the right-hand side is $J_f+\partial_t(\varepsilon_0E+P)=J_f+\partial_tD$, so $\operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$. (c) records the scope: the identities are conditional on the adopted postulates and on $P,M\in C^2$; no constitutive content is used.

current.title: Stationary macroscopic interface jump conditions for D, B, E and H
current.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis under which [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] and the surface conventions of [[def-em-weak-sources]] are stated, and let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]].
Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), let $\sigma_f:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K_f:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K_f(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a free surface charge density and a tangential free surface current density, both stationary in $t$), and let $\rho_v:(\Omega\setminus S)\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $J_v:(\Omega\setminus S)\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Let $E,B,D,H:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$, with the joint one-sided $C^1$ extension property: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side of each field is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder, so that the fields and their first space and time derivatives extend continuously to that side, locally uniformly on compact cylinders. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces.
[Thin-interface hypothesis] Suppose that $E,B,D,H$ satisfy the four macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] in the distributional sense on $U$ with the source pair $\rho_f=\rho_v+\sigma_f\delta_S$, $J_f=J_v+K_f\delta_S$, where the stationary-sheet pairings are those of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) and the equations are $\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$ as identities in the sense of [[def-distribution]], the fields being identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\psi$ ranging over $C_c^\infty(U)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). This thin-interface solution hypothesis is a modelling assumption of the statement: it is the natural weakening of the smooth macroscopic equations to fields with a common stationary discontinuity, and it is not deduced from the smooth-region equations alone.
Then, pointwise on $S\times I$, $$n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,\qquad n\times[H]=K_f,$$ with the Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); equivalently $\sigma_f=n\cdot[D]$ and $K_f=n\times[H]$ recover the free sheet densities from the field jumps.
[Weak-trace branch] If instead of the joint extension hypothesis the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time and, in addition, the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$, then the same four identities hold as identities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t$, and at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify the last upgrade.
[Scope] The interface is stationary, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tD$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic charge and no magnetic surface current are present in the sources; no dipolar sheet layer (a concentrated dipole distribution in $P$ or $M$, which would make the fields non-integrable) is included. No existence theorem for fields with singular sources is asserted, no constitutive law is used, and no empirical claim is made.
current.strategy: **Proof technique:** apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to the four fields and match the coefficients of the surface distribution. By [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ declared), for $C^1$-off-$S$ fields with one-sided $C^1$ traces, $\operatorname{div}D=\{\operatorname{div}D\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[D]\,\delta_S$ and $\operatorname{curl}H=\{\operatorname{curl}H\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[H]\,\delta_S$, with the analogous identities for $B$ and $E$. Substituting into the distributional identities of the hypothesis and using the sheet pairings of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), the regular parts reproduce the off-interface macroscopic equations and the coefficients of $\delta_S$ give, one equation at a time, $n\cdot[D]=\sigma_f$ (from $\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f$), $n\cdot[B]=0$ (from $\operatorname{div}B=0$), $n\times[E]=0$ and $n\times[H]=K_f$: the right-hand sides $\partial_tB$ and $J_f+\partial_tD$ carry no delta term because $S$ is stationary and the joint one-sided $C^1$ hypothesis makes $\partial_tB$ and $\partial_tD$ locally bounded near $S$, hence locally integrable. Since the two-sided traces are continuous on $S\times I$, the distributional coefficient identities are the displayed pointwise identities. The weak-trace branch replaces the pointwise trace argument by the $dS\,dt$-almost-everywhere sheet identity plus the spatial-continuity upgrade. No constitutive relation and no field equation beyond the assumed distributional identities is used.

current.title: Energy balance and Ohmic dissipation for the constant nondispersive linear model
current.statement:
Assume the elementary inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]]: constant symmetric positive-definite matrices $\varepsilon,\mu\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ (isotropic scalar case included) with $D=\varepsilon E$ and $B=\mu H$, and the conduction relation $J_f=\sigma E+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ with $\sigma$ symmetric positive semidefinite and a declared external free current $J_{\mathrm{ext}}$. Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with the regularity hypotheses of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], so that its macroscopic equations hold on $\Omega\times I$. Define the stored-energy density and the energy-flux vector $$u:=\tfrac12\bigl(E\cdot D+B\cdot H\bigr),\qquad S:=E\times H,$$ with the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; $u$ carries $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$ and $S$ carries $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Then:
(a) [Local balance and positivity] On $\Omega\times I$, $$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J_f\cdot E.$$ Moreover $u=\tfrac12(E\cdot\varepsilon E+H\cdot\mu H)\ge0$, with $u(x,t)>0$ whenever $(E(x,t),H(x,t))\ne(0,0)$.
(b) [Dissipation reading] With $J_f=\sigma E+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\sigma$ symmetric positive semidefinite, $E\cdot\sigma E\ge0$ and the balance reads $$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S+E\cdot\sigma E=-J_{\mathrm{ext}}\cdot E;$$ the nonnegative term $E\cdot\sigma E$ is the Ohmic dissipation density of the model.
(c) [Fixed-volume balance] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with $\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let $t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) as in that divergence theorem, and let $n$ be the outward unit normal of $\partial\Omega'$. Then for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$, $$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}u(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\Omega'}J_f\cdot E\,dx-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}S\cdot n\,dS.$$
(d) [Scope] The density $u=\tfrac12(E\cdot D+B\cdot H)$ is a stored-energy density only for this constant symmetric nondispersive model; for general dispersive, nonlocal, nonlinear or hysteretic response no instantaneous stored-energy density is defined or claimed by this item, and the general dispersive work balance is not supplied. The identities hold only where the fields and sources have the stated regularity, the fixed-volume form keeps its boundary term, and no conservation of $\int_{\Omega'}u$ is asserted unless that term vanishes. No empirical claim is made.
current.strategy: **Proof technique:** dot the macroscopic curl equations with the complementary fields and use the cross-product divergence identity. (a): by [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]], $\operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. Taking the Euclidean inner product ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) of the first with $E$ and of the second with $H$ gives $E\cdot\operatorname{curl}H=E\cdot J_f+E\cdot\partial_tD$ and $H\cdot\operatorname{curl}E=-H\cdot\partial_tB$. By [[lem-the-divergence-and-curl-of-a-cross-product]], $\operatorname{div}(E\times H)=H\cdot\operatorname{curl}E-E\cdot\operatorname{curl}H$; subtracting the two scalar equations from this identity gives $\operatorname{div}S+\partial_t\bigl(\tfrac12E\cdot D+\tfrac12B\cdot H\bigr)+J_f\cdot E=0$, because the symmetry of $\varepsilon$ gives $E\cdot\partial_tD=\tfrac12\partial_t(E\cdot\varepsilon E)$ and the symmetry of $\mu$ gives $H\cdot\partial_tB=\tfrac12\partial_t(H\cdot\mu H)$, using $D=\varepsilon E$, $B=\mu H$ and the product rule of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. Positivity is positive definiteness of $\varepsilon,\mu$: $u$ is a sum of two nonnegative quadratic forms, vanishing only when $E=H=0$. (b): $J_f\cdot E=E\cdot\sigma E+J_{\mathrm{ext}}\cdot E$ and $E\cdot\sigma E\ge0$ for symmetric positive semidefinite $\sigma$. (c): [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates $t\mapsto\int_{\Omega'}u$ under the integral sign and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] converts $\int_{\Omega'}\operatorname{div}S$ into the boundary flux; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly the hypothesis of that divergence theorem and is used only in this clause. (d) records the restrictions. No constitutive assumption beyond the declared closure branch, and no empirical premise, is used.

current.title: Period-averaged energy density, Poynting vector and momentum flux of a plane wave
current.statement: Let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega>0$ with $\omega=c|k|$, let $e\in\mathbb C^3$ with $k\cdot e=0$ and $b=k\times e/\omega$, and let $(E,B)$ be the corresponding plane-wave solution of [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]) on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. Let $u$ and $S$ be the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g=S/c^2$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Write $T=2\pi/\omega$, $|e|^2=e\cdot\overline e$, $\hat k=k/|k|$, and let $\langle f\rangle:=\frac1T\int_0^Tf(x,s)\,ds$ be the period average at fixed $x$. Then, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$: (a) [Averaged energy density] $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|e|^2$, independent of $x$ and of the starting time. (b) [Averaged Poynting vector] $\langle S\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2\hat k$; hence $\langle S\rangle=\langle u\rangle c\hat k$, and the period-averaged intensity is $I:=|\langle S\rangle|=c\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}|e|^2$. (c) [Averaged momentum density, stress and momentum flux] $\langle g\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2c}|e|^2\hat k$, and componentwise $\langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle=-\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$, equivalently $\langle\Pi_{ij}\rangle=\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$; the period-averaged momentum flux across a plane with unit normal $n$ is therefore $\langle u\rangle(\hat k\cdot n)\hat k$, a pure flux along $\hat k$ of magnitude $(I/c)(\hat k\cdot n)$. The tensor identity holds for every complex transverse amplitude $e$, not only for real or circular ones. (d) [Balance reading] On the source-free region the local identities of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] hold for this field; since $u,g,S,\sigma$ are $T$-periodic in $t$, the period averages of their time derivatives vanish ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]), so averaging the identities gives $\operatorname{div}\langle S\rangle=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\langle\sigma\rangle=0$ consistently (both averaged fields are in fact constant), and the reading of $u,S,g,\Pi$ as energy and momentum densities and fluxes is that of those two theorems. (e) [Scope] These are exact identities for the ideal plane wave; $I$ is the intensity used by the radiation-pressure thought experiment of the companion page and in radiation-flux arguments. No detection statistics, no finite-beam or finite-time realisation and no empirical claim is made, and the total energy of the wave over $\mathbb R^3$ is infinite rather than finite.
current.strategy: Clause (a)-(c) are the compact-period calculation of [[lem-em-period-average]] applied componentwise: with $E=\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i\theta})$, $B=\operatorname{Re}(b\,e^{i\theta})$, $\theta=k\cdot x-\omega t$, the lemma gives $\langle E_iE_j\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{Re}(e_i\overline{e_j})$, $\langle B_iB_j\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{Re}(b_i\overline{b_j})$ and $\langle(E\times B)_i\rangle=\frac12\operatorname{Re}((e\times\overline b)_i)$; hence $\langle|E|^2\rangle=|e|^2/2$ and, using $b=k\times e/\omega$ and $|k|=\omega/c$, $\langle|B|^2\rangle=|b|^2/2=|e|^2/(2c^2)$. Substituting into $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] and using $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ gives (a) and (b), since $e\times\overline b=e\times(k\times\overline e)/\omega=k|e|^2/\omega$ by the cross-product identity of [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]] and $e\cdot k=0$. For (c), expand $\langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle=(\varepsilon_0/2)\operatorname{Re}(e_i\overline{e_j})-(\varepsilon_0/4)\delta_{ij}|e|^2+(1/(2\mu_0))\operatorname{Re}(b_i\overline{b_j})-(1/(4\mu_0))\delta_{ij}|b|^2$ and substitute $b_ib_j=(k\times e)_i\overline{(k\times e)_j}/\omega^2$ together with the coordinate identity $(k\times e)_i\overline{(k\times e)_j}=|k|^2|e|^2\delta_{ij}-k_ik_j|e|^2-|k|^2e_i\overline{e_j}$ (a bilinear coordinate expansion of the cross product, again from the cited lemma); with $|k|^2/\omega^2=1/c^2$ and $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ all terms combine to $-\langle u\rangle\hat k_i\hat k_j$. Clause (d) averages the balance identities: for the $T$-periodic smooth quantities the mean of the time derivative is zero by the fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]), and the remaining flux terms are the averaged quantities just computed, which are constant and hence divergence-free. No other input is used.

current.title: Ideal absorber and ideal reflector momentum transfer (radiation pressure)
current.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis under which the fixed-volume clause of the momentum balance is stated. Idealised setup: the vacuum region is $\{x_3<0\}$ and a material body occupies $\{x_3>0\}$ with plane surface $x_3=0$; an incident plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] with $k=Ke_3$ ($K>0$, $\omega=cK$), $e=E_0e_1$ ($E_0>0$, unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) and $b=(E_0/c)e_2$ propagates in the $+e_3$ direction. By [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] its period-averaged Poynting flux is $\langle S\rangle=I\hat k$ with $I=\frac{\varepsilon_0c}{2}E_0^2$, and its period-averaged normal Maxwell stress is $\langle\sigma_{33}\rangle=-I/c$ ([[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] for $\sigma$). All period-averaged quantities below are independent of time. Two idealised models of the surface: (i) [Ideal absorber] Adopt (A1) the field on the material side and any reflected field vanish identically, and (A2) the total force on the material is given by the pillbox limit of the momentum balance, i.e. equals, per unit area, the difference $\langle\sigma_{33}(0^+)\rangle-\langle\sigma_{33}(0^-)\rangle$ of the limiting normal stresses on the two sides of the surface. Applying [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b) to a fixed box inside the vacuum region with one face at $x_3=-\delta$ and period-averaging (the time derivative of the averaged field momentum of a periodic configuration has zero mean, [[lem-em-period-average]] for the explicit $\cos^2$-profile) shows $\langle\sigma_{33}\rangle$ is constant in $x_3$ in the vacuum region, so $\langle\sigma_{33}(0^-)\rangle=-I/c$. Then the force per unit area is $F/A=(I/c)\,\hat k$: the wave pushes the absorber along its direction of propagation with pressure $I/c$. (ii) [Ideal reflector] Adopt instead (A1') the field on the material side vanishes identically while the vacuum field is the sum of the incident wave and the reflected plane wave with $k'=-k$, $e'=-e$ (so that the tangential electric field vanishes on $x_3=0$; the sum is a source-free solution by [[pthm-em-linear-superposition]]), together with (A2). Compute the averaged normal stress of the standing wave directly: the real fields satisfy $E=E_0[\cos(Kx_3-\omega t)-\cos(Kx_3+\omega t)]e_1=2E_0\sin(Kx_3)\sin(\omega t)e_1$ and $B=(2E_0/c)\cos(Kx_3)\cos(\omega t)e_2$, whose cross terms cancel identically in $\sigma_{33}=-(\varepsilon_0/2)|E|^2-(1/(2\mu_0))|B|^2$; with $\langle\sin^2\rangle=\langle\cos^2\rangle=1/2$ this gives $\langle\sigma_{33}(0^-)\rangle=-\varepsilon_0E_0^2=-2I/c$ (the incident and reflected waves contribute $-I/c$ each). Hence $F/A=(2I/c)\,\hat k$: twice the absorbing pressure, because the momentum of the reflected wave is reversed. (iii) [Status] The vanishing-field idealisations (A1)/(A1') and the pillbox force law (A2) are adopted model assumptions of this thought experiment, not derived material laws and not observations; the deduction from them with the computed averaged stresses is complete and conditional. The setup idealises an infinite plane beam at normal incidence on an infinite plane surface; oblique incidence, finite beams, real absorbers and any magnetisation/current response of a material require a material model and are excluded. No measured pressure is reported and no empirical or statistical claim is made.
current.strategy: Deduction from the stated idealisations. Incident wave data: $k\times e=KE_0e_2$, so the amplitudes satisfy [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]](b) and (c) of [[pthm-em-wave-energy-average]] gives $I=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2/2$ and $\langle\sigma_{33}\rangle=-I/c$ for a single monochromatic wave. In (i), the vacuum fields are the incident wave alone; the fixed-volume balance [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b) for a box $\{-L<x_3<-\delta\}$ inside the vacuum region (where the field is a smooth source-free solution and $f=0$) with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the period average gives $0=\langle\sigma_{33}(-\delta)\rangle-\langle\sigma_{33}(-L)\rangle$, so the limiting value at $0^-$ is $-I/c$; the force law (A2) then gives $F/A=-(-I/c)=I/c$ along $+e_3$. In (ii), the standing-wave fields are computed explicitly and averaged with [[lem-em-period-average]]; the cross terms cancel identically in $\sigma_{33}$ because $|E|^2$ and $(c^2)$-weighted $|B|^2$ have opposite cross terms for the two counterpropagating waves, leaving $-\varepsilon_0E_0^2(-2I/c)$ at $0^-$, whence $F/A=2I/c$ by (A2). The real-vector trig identities and the substitution $\cos A\pm\cos B$, $\sin A\pm\sin B$ are elementary; the averaged squares use $\langle\cos^2\rangle=\langle\sin^2\rangle=1/2$ from [[lem-em-period-average]]. The direction $\hat k$ is $e_3$, the propagation direction of the incident beam. No material law, absorbed or reflected amplitude, or observed force is derived.
current.physical_scope: Adopted idealisations of a plane beam at normal incidence on an infinite plane ideal absorber or ideal reflector, with the pillbox force law as an explicitly stated model assumption; the conclusion is the conditional pressure $I/c$ or $2I/c$ along the propagation direction. Excluded: oblique incidence, finite beams and pulses, real material response, radiation reaction, measurements, and any empirical claim; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is declared for the fixed-volume balance clause.
